system.summary: Two-digit numbers 10-99 = letters in bands of 3 homophones; numbers 100-3999 = alphabetical nomenclator (about one code per word); abbreviations for common words; clear words interspersed.

prior_solution.where: Two clear copies of the time follow the ciphered letter (fol. 102 signed D. v. F., fol. 103); Dittmar and Kirchhoff discuss the letter (Dittmar wrongly says it was not deciphered). Found after the first reading. Daniel's leads 1126 and 1127 only (the vetting of 1126 already records the clear copies, from our corrections of 29 Oct 2026); nothing else in this repository.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout set the rules (protocol hashed before any key was built, one held-out measurement). An AI agent transcribed, harvested the glosses, built K1/K2, measured and read; no human palaeographer.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agent run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Ciphered letter of 28 March 1631 transcribed (parts 1 and 2); gloss pairs of the neighbouring letters collected.
K1 built on the interlinear glosses of the other letters (images 112-132) with the letter of 17 March set aside; frozen.
Held-out letter of 17 March: letters 39/43 = 0.907, codes 22/24 = 0.917 by the frozen script; best of 200 permuted keys 0.233 / 0.125; thresholds 0.85 / 0.75 fixed beforehand.
Letter of 28 March read with K2: about 80 % of 172 tokens by sense; then the clear copies on images 134-135 were found, 21 of 25 restorations confirmed.
K2 on a second held-out letter (22 Jan 1631): too few glossed lines, inconclusive.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Key learnt on the interlinear glosses of the neighbouring letters of the same volume; the letter itself has two clear copies of the time.

validation.notes: K1: letters 39/43 = 0.907, codes 22/24 = 0.917 by the frozen script (24/24 after two normalisation misses) on the held-out letter of 17 March; controls 0.233 / 0.125.

outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.md: 172 cipher tokens before the clear copy was found: strict count 92 sure (0.535); with 20 probable 0.651; with 25 restored 0.797; 35 unresolved. The content is existing (two clear copies of the time).

credits.note: two clear copies of the letter on the images that follow it (fol. 102-103)
letter found, K1 built and validated, the cipher read to about 80 % by sense before the clear copy was seen

texts.label: Falkenberg to Gustavus Adolphus, 28 March 1631
texts.summary: Falkenberg reports from Magdeburg that the situation has changed, asks for a general relief and not small troops, says supplies are short and the town cannot hold long beyond Easter, and describes the country on the Elbe (Garleben, Saltwedel).

reading_review.note: strict count 53.5 % sure (79.7 % with probable and restored); 4 of 25 restorations wrong against the clear copy; content existing

outcome.notes: No image is reproduced (Public Domain Mark would allow it). decryption.txt is a quick reading of the clear copy, not a full edition.
